messages:
jane_cust: Hey — customer reported their client started failing JSON.parse on our streaming response after ~15s. They say it was fine before but recently started hitting truncation mid-object.

jane_cust: They pasted the raw stream tail from their collector:```json
data: {"request_id":"req-9a2", "choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...updates"}} , {"delta":{"content":" more"}} , {"delta":{"content":" end"}}]
data: {"request_id":"req-9a2", "choices":[{"delta":{"content":"unexpected"}}
```

maria (Support): Thanks — can you also grab the raw bytes/hex from the collector around the cutoff? Curious if it's 0-length chunk or premature connection close.

jane_cust: Pasted chunk dump (from their edge):
```
# CHUNK 42 len=1024 seq=42
{"id":"req-9a2","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"...updates"}}]}
# CHUNK 43 len=12 seq=43
,{"delta":{"content":" more"}}
# CHUNK 44 len=8 seq=44
,{"delta":{"content":" end"}}
# CHUNK 45 len=6 seq=45

(truncated mid-chunk)
```
ingest-proxy-bot: Observed oddity — ingress reported reorder: seq 43 delivered before 42 to collector at 12:34:56Z. Also saw HTTP/2 stream multiplexing reset on upstream connection id=7.

ryan (SRE): This looks like chunk boundary reordering across TCP connections or a proxy that buffers and re-emits partial chunks out of order. We had a similar class with http2->http1.1 conversion on an old nginx + upstream keepalive bug.

eng-oliver: Can you confirm the customer is using a terminating proxy (LB) that does HTTP/2 on client side and HTTP/1.1 to our edge? If so, nginx buffer and proxy_request_buffering settings commonly cause split/reorder.

jane_cust: Customer says they have a managed LB (belongs to partner) and they do h2->h1 transcode. They enabled proxy buffering recently in a config change two days ago.

maria (Support): Repro steps requested. Can customer run a curl against our /v1/stream endpoint with -N and show raw output? Suggested command:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=x --http2
```

jane_cust: Ran it through their LB and got interleaved frames. Raw dump:```
data: {"id":"req-9a2","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hel"}}}
data: {"id":"req-9a2","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"lo"}}}
data: ,{"delta":{"content":" world"}}
```

ryan (SRE): Repro locally by running an http2 multiplexer + proxy with proxy_buffering on + small proxy_buffers. I can try to simulate with h2load + local envoy.

eng-oliver: Short-term mitigation: customer can set X-Accel-Buffering: no / disable buffering on their LB or use a TCP passthrough mode. Long-term: we should add chunk-sequence metadata on each SSE/data frame so downstream can detect reorder/truncation more gracefully.

maria (Support): Next steps: 1) jane_cust to ask partner LB to disable request/response buffering for this route and test. 2) ryan to run a local repro with envoy/nginx and attach pcap. 3) eng-oliver to scope adding per-frame sequence header (eng ticket).

jane_cust: Will ask partner and report back. Thanks.

ryan (SRE): I started a quick repro script and hit the same behavior with envoy when enabling response_buffering and HTTP/2 upstream multiplexing — attaching logs to the thread (will upload).

eng-oliver: Filed ENG-1972 to add sequence id header (X-Redwood-Frame-Seq) + a runtime flag to include it in SSE. Can help with API compat notes.

maria (Support): Marking as escalation -> severity: minor for now (customer can workaround), owner: eng-oliver, SRE contact: ryan. Please update this thread with status. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy finished: add-frame-seq-flag -> staging @ 1945012405

jane_cust: Partner disabled buffering and stream now completes cleanly for 2/2 attempts. Resolving on customer side for now, will hold for ENG-1972.

maria (Support): Great — closing loop with customer and tracking ENG ticket. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
